## Rotate the Password

To change `password` without signing everyone out, keep the old one in `extraUnsealPasswords`. Extra passwords only open sessions; new seals always use `password`.

```js
const session = await useSession(event, {
  password: process.env.SESSION_PASSWORD_NEW, // seals every new session
  extraUnsealPasswords: [process.env.SESSION_PASSWORD_OLD], // only opens existing ones
});
```

1. Move the current password to `extraUnsealPasswords` and set the new one as `password`.
2. Cookie sessions opened by an extra password are resealed with `password` on their next request, so they migrate on their own.
3. Once the sessions have migrated (after `maxAge`, for example), remove the old password from the list.

`password` is tried first, then each extra password in order, so list the most recent one first. Extra passwords need the same entropy as `password` (at least 32 random characters).

> [!NOTE]
> Sessions sent through the `x-{name}-session` header cannot be resealed, so they keep opening with the old password for as long as it stays in the list.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Each extra password costs one more PBKDF2 derivation for a cookie that does not open, so keep the list short. An old password that was compromised keeps opening sessions until you remove it.
